_id: carr rung: the Melbourne-Wubbena wide lane, formed from the REAL observables, on ONE asset. This is the rung carr014 was mistaken for. carr014 rotates the EKF's ambiguity COVARIANCE through D = [1/lam1, -1/lam2; 1/lam1, 1/lam2] and never touches a code observable, so what it reports is a property of P and it inherits P's blind direction. The Melbourne-Wubbena combination is a DATA combination whose precision comes from code noise over the arc and is independent of P entirely. The two numbers have unrelated origins and only one of them is the wide lane the theory chapter routes the cascade through. This rung measures that one.
_delta: diagnostics.melbourneWubbena.enable true (was false). Nothing else. The estimator emits no z/h/H/R row and returns nothing to the filter, so every EKF metric must come out bit-identical to the reference: a non-zero difference in position, clock or NIS is a defect in the gating, not a result.
_WHYTHISNEEDSNOSECONDSATELLITE: MW = (f1*L1 - f2*L2)/(f1-f2) - (f1*P1 + f2*P2)/(f1+f2) = lam_WL*N_WL + eps. Range, both clocks, the troposphere and the first-order ionosphere cancel INSIDE the combination. No differencing is required for any of that. The claim that this repository's wide lane needs two satellites was a statement about revgnss.GroundCarrierAmbiguityResolver, which parameterises one ambiguity per (satellite i>=2, tower, arc) because it was built for the ORIENTATION problem. That is implementation scope, not physics.
_ANDWHYITSTILLDIFFERENCESBETWEENTOWERS: Undifferenced MW is not an integer in this simulation, for two reasons that are both configuration rather than physics. errors.interAntennaCarrierBias is keyed (antenna, signal) INDEPENDENT of tower and enters at 0.25*sqrt(2) = 0.354 wide-lane cycles on antennas 2..4. biases.interFrequency.code is global per signal and enters at (f1*0.30 + f2*0.45)/(f1+f2)/lam_WL = 0.424 wide-lane cycles. Both are constant across towers, so a between-tower single difference removes them identically, and one asset sees five towers.
_WHATSURVIVESTHEDIFFERENCE_CORRECTED: An earlier version of this file said the surviving residual was the per-tower code hardware delay at 0.05 m = 0.058 wide-lane cycles, times sqrt(2) for the difference. THAT IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN: on the resolved config errors.hardwareDelay.truth.default_m is 0, truth.perTower is absent and perTowerBias.enable is 0, so there is NO deterministic per-tower delay at all. Only residualStochastic is on, at sigma 0.05 m, and being stochastic it averages down rather than surviving as an offset. Auditing every truth term that survives BOTH the MW combination and the between-tower difference, the only DETERMINISTIC one left is higher-order ionosphere, measured at 0.0025 wide-lane cycles after differencing. Everything else that survives -- code multipath, code scintillation, the hardware-delay residual -- is zero-mean and therefore averages, so meanAbsFractionalPart is NOT a bias and the label 'the leftover BIAS' on it is wrong.
_THENUMBERTOREADFIRSTISNOTTHESIGMA: It is whiteOverstatement. The dominant MW error here is coloured -- errors.multipath.coloredGM.tau_s is 60 s and, with sharedAcrossAntennas on, ONE chain serves every antenna of a tower -- so an arc mean does NOT improve as 1/sqrt(n). The estimator MEASURES its own covariance by batch means instead of asserting a noise model, and reports what a 1/sqrt(n) implementation would have claimed. On a 3600 s arc at tau = 60 s the predicted overstatement is sqrt(T/2tau) = 5.5x. If the measured ratio comes back near that, it is a direct confirmation that the naive covariance every textbook MW implementation uses is wrong by a factor of five in this error model, which is a finding in its own right and is the reason the covariance is measured rather than assumed.
_WHATWOULDMAKETHISUNSAFETOQUOTE: A wide-lane sigma quoted as though it settled the geometry. The combination is geometry-free, which is exactly why a good sigma here says NOTHING about whether the position underneath is good enough for anything else. The thesis already carries a worked example of that inference going wrong: test008 fixed twenty of twenty wide-lane components at a bootstrapped rate of 1.000 while the orientation solve it fed was wrong by a factor of twenty-one. Report the wide lane as a statement about AMBIGUITY OBSERVABILITY and nothing more.
_WINDUPLEAKISVACUOUSHERE: windupLeakMax_m reads 0.000e+00 on THIS rung and that particular number proves nothing, because errors.phaseWindup.enable resolves to FALSE on golden_baseline and the per-row wind-up the estimator reads is therefore identically zero. The CANCELLATION ITSELF IS ESTABLISHED, just not by this rung: (a) algebraically, since wind-up is constant in cycles so the wide-lane phase combination sees (f1*lam1 - f2*lam2)*w/(f1-f2) and f1*lam1 = f2*lam2 = c; (b) in floating point, where f1*(c/f1) and f2*(c/f2) both round to EXACTLY c in double precision, so exact zero is the correct result rather than a machine-epsilon residue; (c) at runtime on a dedicated 120 s run with errors.phaseWindup.enable true, which reported phaseWindupNLinks 40 and a span of 0.0823 cycles across links with the MW leak still exactly zero. Cite (c), never this rung's zero.
_MEASURED_2700s_PILOT: A 2700 s pilot of this exact config (nReceivers 4, default 300 s blocks, 9 blocks, 16 arcs) gave: WL float sigma 0.1019 cycles (0.0878 m); mean |fractional part| 0.2077 cycles. A 1/sqrt(n) covariance would have claimed 0.0246 cycles, i.e. 4.10x optimistic. THE sqrt(T/2tau) = 4.74x BENCHMARK THAT NUMBER WAS ONCE JUDGED AGAINST IS WITHDRAWN: it is a dimensional error, conflating N_eff = T/(2tau) with N = T/dt. The ratio measured here estimates sqrt(1 + 2*sum rho_k), which for AR(1) with dt << tau tends to sqrt(2*tau/dt) = 10.95 and is INDEPENDENT OF ARC LENGTH -- the tell is that the wrong formula contains no dt. Read correctly the measurement is a result rather than a shortfall: a ratio of 3.891 against a realised inflation near 96 puts the coloured multipath at about 15 percent of the MW variance and white code thermal plus phase at about 85 percent.
_THERESIDUALISNOTABIAS: meanAbsFractionalPart falls with arc length -- 0.2077 at 2700 s, 0.1332 at 3600 s, 0.1162 at 7200 s -- which a constant offset cannot do. Combined with the audit above showing no deterministic term above 0.0025 cycles survives the difference, the honest reading is that this quantity is coloured noise that has not finished averaging, not a bias. IT IS HOWEVER ABOUT 2x LARGER THAN THE REPORTED SIGMA PREDICTS: for zero-mean noise E|x| = 0.798*sigma, giving 0.0696 at 3600 s against a measured 0.1332, and 0.0535 at 7200 s against 0.1162. So the batch-mean covariance is optimistic by roughly a factor of two, which matters more than any bias would: P(success) is computed from it.
_MEASURED_THEHEADLINE: 16 of 16 wide-lane components round to the correct integer, against 7 of 20 for the undifferenced twin carr018. That contrast IS the result of this pair. Note that the class still REFUSED to fix, on the ratio test (1.18 against a threshold of 2.0), while the bootstrap success rate read 0.999543. A ratio near 1 means the second-best integer vector is almost as good as the best, which is the signature of an unmodelled bias rather than of insufficient precision, so the refusal is correct and the bootstrap number alone would have been misleading.
_THESECONDTHINGTOREAD: meanAbsFractionalPart. In betweenTower mode it should collapse toward the surviving per-tower hardware delay. Run the twin with mode 'undifferenced' and it should jump to roughly the quadrature sum of the inter-antenna bias and the DCB quoted above. That pair of numbers MEASURES the bias budget instead of asserting it, and it is the cheapest available check that the differencing is doing what this file claims.
_reportNote: compileTex 'auto' rather than the golden's 'require': a ladder rung's deliverable is its .mat, and a pdflatex hiccup must not throw away a finished run.
